purpose: rc namespace table: the exit codes of the M-card runners are NOT comparable across runner versions
hard_rule: Never aggregate, average, count or compare raw rc values across cards without naming the runner sha256 that produced them. The same integer has different meanings in different runner generations (2 = harness failure in one, 2 = 'no verdict could be issued' in another).

M17-M20 a20260919-01.runner_sha256_note: both values are byte-identical across the four attempts; the change was
the P2-1 fix (per-case declared expectation enforced by exact type

exit_codes.1: harness error (the runner itself could not produce a verdict)
exit_codes.2: no verdict: the frozen expectation is missing, or the observed output cannot be faithfully compared with the frozen shape
exit_codes.3: negative verdict: positive raised/out of tolerance, continuity positive did not match, or at least one negative case was not rejected as its DECLARED expectation requires

M17-M20 a20260919-01.declared_expectation_enforcement: yes (post-review P2-1): the raised exception's EXACT type name must equal cases.json's per-case 'expected' string; compared by type name, never by isinstance, because ModelRegistryError is a ValueError subclass

exit_codes.3: negative verdict (positive mismatch, continuity failure or unrejected negative)
exit_codes.1: not defined by that runner; a bare 1 there is not a harness-error signal

M05-M08 a20260919-01.declared_expectation_enforcement: no: that runner recorded cases.json's 'expected' but did not compare it
M05-M08 a20260919-01.note: read from that attempt's own artefacts; this batch did not modify it

M21-M31.exit_codes: NOT VERIFIED BY THIS BATCH - do not infer them from either namespace above

why_this_table_exists: the independent review of M17-M20 found that the same defect (per-case declared expectation never compared) had been found independently in M21-M24, i.e. the harness is shared across batches; without a namespace table a cross-card rc aggregate would silently misclassify harness failures as negative verdicts
